title: Detecting tool support in OpenRouter
body:
### 📦 Platform

Official Cloud, Self hosting Docker

### 📦 Deploymenet mode

client db (lobe-chat image)

### 📌 Version

1.136.4

### 💻 Operating System

Windows

### 🌐 Browser

Firefox

### 🐛 Bug Description

I believe there's an issue with the way tool support is determined for OpenRouter models.

It seems we currently use the API at `https://openrouter.ai/api/frontend/models` to get the models.
This endpoint is undocumented and it appears that OpenRouter use it specifically for their website's [model comparator](https://openrouter.ai/compare).
Lobe Chat uses a field from this API called `supports_tool_parameters` to determine if tools are supported in a model:

```json
"endpoint": {
  "supports_tool_parameters": false
}
```

But the issue is that the `endpoint` field only returns capabilities of the first provider for a model.

For example, the first provider for `deepseek-r1-0528` is _Chutes_ and it doesn't support tools for the model.
But the forth provider for `deepseek-r1-0528` is _SiliconFlow_ and is does support tools for the same model.

The result is that `deepseek-r1-0528` is detected in Lobe Chat as a model without tool support (unless a user manually re-enable it).

---

However OpenRouter actually provides a documented API for this exact purpose.
It's located at `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models` and documented [here](https://openrouter.ai/docs/api-reference/list-available-models).
It also doesn't require authentication to use.

This API is well aware that `deepseek-r1-0528` support tools:

```json
"supported_parameters": [
  "frequency_penalty",
  "include_reasoning",
  "logit_bias",
  "logprobs",
  "max_tokens",
  "min_p",
  "presence_penalty",
  "reasoning",
  "repetition_penalty",
  "response_format",
  "seed",
  "stop",
  "structured_outputs",
  "temperature",
  "tool_choice",
  "tools",
  "top_k",
  "top_logprobs",
  "top_p"
]
```

The `tools` parameter indicates that the model support tools.
This is actually specifically called out in the docs:

> Note: `supported_parameters` is a union of all parameters supported by all providers for this model.

I think this API is the suitable source to get this kind of data instead of what's currently used.

### 📷 Recurrence Steps

Fetch up-to-date models from OpenRouter.

### 🚦 Expected Behavior

Models would be tagged with their actual capabilities supported on OpenRouter.

### 📝 Additional Information

_No response_

## Summary by Sourcery

Optimize the OpenRouter modelFetch endpoint by migrating to the v1 API, flattening the response schema, and improving model metadata extraction

Enhancements:
- Switch OpenRouter model fetch URL to the v1 endpoint
- Restructure model mapping and type definitions to align with the new API schema (top_provider, architecture)
- Enhance displayName parsing by stripping vendor prefixes and duplicate segments
- Extract pricing, token limits, and feature flags (functionCall, reasoning, vision) from the flattened schema fields

ai_judgment.response: Yes. This is an agent issue because it involves tool invocation and configuration errors. The issue highlights incorrect detection of tool support for models due to reliance on an undocumented API, which affects the agent's ability to determine and utilize tools properly.
